ui_scenarios.name: WASD movement feel is acceptable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires player judgment about speed, acceleration, and spatial feel.

ui_scenarios.name: Mouse-look feel is acceptable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires player judgment about sensitivity and comfort.

ui_scenarios.name: Escape opens settings and settings close returns to captured mouse
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks cover panel state and requested mouse mode; human review must confirm OS-level mouse capture and click feel in the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Completed interaction polish pass feels readable across prompts, carry, placement, workstations, and settings
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human review of the full repeated first-person workflow after the Stop 3 interaction pass.

ui_scenarios.name: Click prompt hierarchy readability is acceptable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment that action, subject, blocked, hover, landing, and feedback prompt states stay readable across real player angles.

ui_scenarios.name: Center reticle action and feedback readability is acceptable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment while aiming at receiving items, shelf slots, the register, the backroom computer, and blocked held-item actions.

ui_scenarios.name: Receiving box, display rack, register, and used-game placement makes sense
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human composition review while graybox layout is changing.

ui_scenarios.name: Store lighting keeps sales floor, register, prompts, reticle, and backroom readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify lighting layers and screenshot sanity; human review must judge readability from the actual player camera.

ui_scenarios.name: Fictional store and zone signage is readable and not mistaken for real brands or interaction targets
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify label text and nonblocking placement; human review must confirm signs compose clearly in the game window.

ui_scenarios.name: Retail posters, price tag, bargain bin, mat, and small display props add identity without hiding click targets
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify nonblocking placement and short callouts; human review must confirm clutter does not obscure prompts or product readability.

ui_scenarios.name: Held item stack pose and motion stay visible without blocking normal navigation
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify pose bounds and motion constraints; human review must confirm the carry stack feels natural while moving and looking around the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Stocking one carried game leaves the remaining carried games visible and usable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that the carry stack reads naturally during movement and after one item is stocked.

ui_scenarios.name: Stocked game is compact, upright, and intentional in the rack
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment from several player angles; automated checks cover dimensions but not whether the case reads at the right scale in the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Used-game case cue details read as boxed-game affordances without overwhelming prompts
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify cue existence and bounds; human review must judge visual clarity in receiving, rack, carry, and customer-held contexts.

ui_scenarios.name: Display rack reads as a used-game rack after category assignment changes
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that metadata changes did not make stocking behavior or visual intent confusing.

ui_scenarios.name: Rack category header and slot rails clarify stocking affordance without reading as separate interactions
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify header and rail placement; human review must confirm the added affordances do not distract from shelf-slot prompts.

ui_scenarios.name: Receiving intake lanes and label organize physical stock without hiding starter items or optional artifacts
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify nonblocking lanes and label; human review must confirm item, note, and serial-mismatch readability from player angles.

ui_scenarios.name: Pricing panel text and controls are readable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about UI readability and control clarity.

ui_scenarios.name: Apply-to-matching pricing option is readable and understandable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about whether the batch-pricing option is clear in the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Pricing panel closes back into first-person mouse capture cleanly
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires OS/window-level input judgment beyond current automated checks.

ui_scenarios.name: Screenshot composition is useful, not merely nonblank
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment; automated gate only checks dimensions and nonblank pixels.

ui_scenarios.name: Current screenshots are reviewed as prototype gaps before production art work begins
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human production-direction judgment; the current build can validate mechanically while still needing the larger game-completion phase.

ui_scenarios.name: First-view screenshot is reviewed against the production small-game-store target
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human composition judgment against the production target contract; automated screenshot checks only prove image presence and dimensions.

ui_scenarios.name: Visual target contract matches the intended stylized fictional game-store tone
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human art-direction judgment before production scene slices replace graybox surfaces.

ui_scenarios.name: Starter layout contract keeps storefront, sales floor, register, and backroom workflows physically readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human production review because automated layout checks cannot judge the intended small-store composition yet.

ui_scenarios.name: Completed environment pass reads as a small game store while preserving the current playable loop
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human review of storefront, sales floor, register, fixture, backroom, lighting, screenshot composition, and movement readability after the environment production pass.

ui_scenarios.name: Production UI contract covers prompt, pricing, register, trade-in, computer, ordering, release, and report decisions
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human UX review before replacing the current functional prototype panels with production UI.

ui_scenarios.name: Production UI text size, contrast, keyboard/mouse focus, and 1280x720 panel fit are readable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify the shared accessibility floor; human review must confirm perceived readability, focus behavior, and no clipping in the actual game window.

ui_scenarios.name: Production content contract is broad enough for several days of fictional data-driven play
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human product review to confirm the target catalog, customer, supplier, event, and unlock scope before implementation.

ui_scenarios.name: Product schema metadata reads like useful game-store inventory data
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify field presence and coverage; human review should confirm category, platform family, format, condition, completeness, authenticity, rarity, demand, value, risk, and location choices feel coherent for fictional game-store products.

ui_scenarios.name: Product visual variants read as distinct inventory forms without becoming clutter
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify variant-rule coverage and cue-node visibility; human review should confirm case, disc, cartridge, accessory, console, controller, box, sealed, loose, and service-ticket cues are readable at receiving, hand, shelf, customer, and register scale.

ui_scenarios.name: Starter catalog breadth feels sufficient for several fictional store days
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify count and category coverage; human review should confirm the used-game, new-game, accessory, hardware, and service-ticket names/prices feel coherent and not repetitive.

ui_scenarios.name: Product condition and authenticity cues are readable but not noisy
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify scratches, missing manual, loose media, damaged label, reseal, and serial-risk cue meshes; human review should confirm they read clearly at gameplay scale without overwhelming product identity.

ui_scenarios.name: Product shelf labels and price tags are readable without cluttering interaction targets
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify compact category, platform, price, sale, preorder, staff-pick, and bargain text; human review should confirm world-space label scale and density work in receiving, hand, shelf, customer, and register contexts.

ui_scenarios.name: Product pipeline validation manifest matches the current content checker and manual review scope
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify the manifest shape, command, covered paths, and requirements; human review should confirm it remains the right content-quality bar before adding more product resources.

ui_scenarios.name: Buyers visibly wait at the register after stocking Star Trader copies
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about queue placement and readability in the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Multiple queued buyers have readable spacing and use a clear lane at the register
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks enforce spacing from special customers; human review confirms the queue reads naturally from the playable camera.

ui_scenarios.name: Buyers visibly walk from browsing to rack to register without clipping badly
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment about movement readability and clipping while the graybox layout is changing.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer idle, walk, browse, pickup, queue, talk, payment, handoff, leave, and impatient poses read clearly
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify the pose-state contract; human review must confirm the placeholder motion reads naturally in the actual game window.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer spawn, approach, and queue positions read naturally in the current layout
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about customer path composition beyond bounded automated path checks.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer browsing, register approach, blocked-path recovery, and leaving behavior read naturally
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify bounded path points and state transitions; human review must confirm the route reads naturally in the production store layout.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer feedback bubbles for price refusal, purchase intent, impatience, trade-in, preorder, service, and suspicion are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify bubble presence and outcome tones; human review must confirm world-space text is readable without cluttering the player view.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer archetypes feel distinct enough to support browser, buyer, parent, collector, trade-in, return, service, regular, and suspicious roles
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify data coverage and scene wiring; human review must judge whether the roles match the intended production customer mix.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer help, recommendation, trade-in pushback, complaint, and hidden-thread probe dialogue feels useful and nonblocking
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify dialogue-flow data coverage; human review must judge tone, usefulness, and whether hidden-thread probes stay optional.

ui_scenarios.name: Register sale completion message is readable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about prompt/message readability during checkout.

ui_scenarios.name: Register checkout receipt, tender, change due, return placeholder, and confirmation controls are readable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that the new register checkout panel fits the game window and reads as a register surface during repeated sale, preorder, and service workflows.

ui_scenarios.name: Trade-in seller and carried game are readable at the register without obvious floating or clipping
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated compact-anchor checks cover pose bounds; human review confirms the game appears held against the seller and does not clip through the register counter.

ui_scenarios.name: Buyer, preorder, trade-in, service, and suspicious customers are visually separated enough to understand their roles
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated spacing catches obvious overlaps, but human review must confirm the register area reads naturally from the playable camera.

ui_scenarios.name: Customer torso, headwear, arms, legs, props, and role silhouettes read as people rather than capsules
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated checks verify the modular body kit exists; human review must confirm the stylized shapes read clearly from normal player angles.

ui_scenarios.name: Trade-in register prompt and completion message are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about prompt/message readability during the trade-in.

ui_scenarios.name: Trade-in offer panel condition, demand, market, and accept/decline controls are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about panel readability and whether the offer review is understandable.

ui_scenarios.name: Preorder register prompt and completion message are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about whether the register flow clearly reads as a deposit rather than a sale.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom preorder count and deposit total are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about whether preorder obligation text fits comfortably in the management panel.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom computer placement is readable and does not look like a second register
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual judgment about prop placement and terminal identity.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom receiving, storage, management, service/paperwork, and movement zones are visually distinct
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human composition review from normal player angles after the backroom spatial polish pass.

ui_scenarios.name: Receiving pallet, delivery door, invoice clipboard, storage shelf, backstock overflow, and labels make delivered stock read as physical inventory
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that receiving, storage, supplier stock, and pending fixture identity add clarity without blocking interaction.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom service, management, safe, security, and evidence-locker props read as context, not new active terminals
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that service, management, and future hidden-thread placeholders support the theme while current register and hidden-thread behavior remain unchanged.

ui_scenarios.name: Day summary panel text and controls are readable in the actual window
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about summary readability and mouse capture behavior.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom computer actions are grouped as Supplier, Storage, Release, Day, and Storage Placement controls
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that grouped button labels, including fixture Cancel, read clearly in the actual game window and do not imply register work belongs on the backroom computer.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom computer dashboard, inventory, ordering, releases, reports, services, storage, suppliers, settings, and records tabs are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify tab existence and section visibility; human review must confirm the tab grid fits the actual window, communicates the computer information architecture, and keeps register work out of the backroom surface.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom category demand readout is readable and does not crowd the panel
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify the demand text exists; the player must judge whether the expanded backroom panel is visually comfortable.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom market drift readout is readable and understandable
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify market drift text exists; the player must judge whether current and drifted market values are readable.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom summary numbers match completed single and multiple sales
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human confirmation after playing through single-sale and multi-sale loops.

ui_scenarios.name: Closed-day report cash, sales, trade-ins, services, preorders, launch activity, reputation, losses, bills, and tomorrow recommendations are readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify report text; human review must confirm the expanded end-of-day report fits the actual window and matches a played day.

ui_scenarios.name: Backroom inventory summary is readable and matches visible active inventory
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human comparison between the summary panel and visible stocked/receiving items.

ui_scenarios.name: Sold item is no longer visually available on the rack after checkout
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human visual confirmation from normal player angles.

ui_scenarios.name: Fixture ghost valid and invalid states are visually readable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about whether translucent green and red placement previews are clear in the actual window.

ui_scenarios.name: Fixture movement, rotate, snap, cancel, and placement controls feel predictable
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment about whether backroom panel movement, fixed-step rotation, grid snap, cancel/refund, and placement confirmation feel understandable before placing a storage rack.

ui_scenarios.name: Suspicious event flags do not visibly interrupt normal store progression
ui_scenarios.reason: The hidden-thread event log is intentionally infrastructure-only for now; human playtest should confirm no new visible story UI appeared.

ui_scenarios.name: Mismatched serial item is discoverable without blocking normal inventory flow
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human confirmation that the optional suspicious copy can still be picked up, priced, stocked, sold, and inspected without feeling like a required story step.

ui_scenarios.name: Supplier message artifact is readable and clearly optional
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human judgment that the receiving note placement and text read as an optional clue rather than a blocking objective.

ui_scenarios.name: Supplier ordering card details are readable and make clear that orders arrive as physical receiving stock
ui_scenarios.reason: Automated tests verify category, cart, cost, delivery, storage, and receiving text; human review must confirm the backroom ordering tab fits the actual game window and does not imply instant inventory teleporting.

ui_scenarios.name: Evidence storage remains hidden during normal play
ui_scenarios.reason: Requires human confirmation that hidden evidence infrastructure did not add a visible objective, warning, or panel before a deliberate UI slice.
